subfigures.description: One continuous U-shaped/bent tube, with a short left arm and tall right arm; no separate initial-state panel is drawn.

pixelFacts.description: The left and right arms are joined by a rounded lower bend. The short left arm has a rounded closing cap. The tall right arm ends in a small oval rim. No valves, taps, screw joints, separate reservoirs, gauges, stands, ruler or hidden connections are visible.

A dark filled region is continuous through the lower bend. Its left surface is low in the short arm; its right surface is much higher in the long arm. Unfilled tube space is visible above both surfaces.

Two approximately horizontal guide strokes identify the upper right fluid level and the lower left fluid level; the lower guide crosses toward the right. At their right ends is a vertical two-ended height marker, with arrowhead-like ends directed toward the guide levels. The single visible variable label is italic h, rotated in the source.

textSupportedInterpretation.fluidIdentity: Mercury, from the independently approved original/current bilingual text, not from the black fill alone.
textSupportedInterpretation.trappedSpace: A fixed mass of air trapped in the short capped arm, from the approved text.
textSupportedInterpretation.historicalContext: Boyle historical apparatus only; no construction, handling or operation instructions for children.
textSupportedInterpretation.numericalAccount: The text describes an initially equal-level state and a later 760 mm height difference under the book's atmospheric-pressure assumption, with absolute pressure doubling and gas volume halving. Those numbers are not printed or calibrated in this source image and must not become invented figure readings.
textSupportedInterpretation.pressureMeaning: Absolute pressure, not gauge pressure, in the approved lesson.

uncertainties: The rim and lower arrowhead are coarse raster strokes; redraw only the visible rim and double-ended marker, without inventing hidden components.
Tube dimensions, cross-section, exact fluid heights, trapped volume and temperature are uncalibrated. No numeric ratios may be inferred from pixel distances.
A tiny isolated dark fleck at the far right is not a legible label, point or quantity; do not convert raster noise into instructional content.
